key_insight: Epitaxial 0.5PZT-0.5PFN thin films show a strong, reversible polarization-dependent photocurrent, linking ferroelectric state to photovoltaic response in a single multiferroic layer.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a route to self-powered optoelectronic and memory devices where light response can be tuned or read out by ferroelectric polarization.
method: Pulsed laser deposition of 0.5Pb(Zr0.52Ti0.48)O3-0.5Pb(Fe0.5Nb0.5)O3 on SrTiO3(001) with SrRuO3 bottom electrode
Confirmed single-phase, highly oriented (001) perovskite film structure
Measured ferroelectric, magnetic, and monochromatic photocurrent responses
evidence_signal: The films showed remanent polarization around 17 μC/cm², coercive field around 150 kV/cm, weak ferromagnetism at room temperature, and polarization-dependent Jsc up to ±20 μA/cm² under 403 nm illumination.
watch_item: The reported photoresponse is demonstrated under monochromatic laser illumination, so scaling to broadband sunlight, long-term stability, and device integration still needs validation.
paper_title: Enhanced Photocurrent Response in Epitaxial 0.5PZT-0.5PFN Multiferroic Thin Films
